title: Explain a Trade-off against Shared Criteria
status: New proposed Lesson 08 production script, 2026-10-30. No new animation or narration in this handoff.
learningOutcome: Explain the purpose and cost of a candidate arrangement against the same criteria without inventing outcome evidence or an agreed timetable.

scenario.kind: Original fictional discussion-training case with explicitly named snapshots
scenario.sourcePrompt: A community book club wants a 30-minute taster activity for new readers. Help them try discussing a short text and find out how the weekly club works. Your group should recommend one coherent activity and explain how it serves both aims. Use the main room, the supplied one-page text and club information sheet, and existing paper and pens; do not buy anything. Leave at least five minutes within the session for visitors' questions.

facts.text: The task is one coherent 30-minute taster activity, serving both trying a short-text discussion and learning how the weekly club works.
The main room, one supplied one-page text, a club information sheet, paper and pens are available. No purchases are allowed. At least five minutes for questions is included within the thirty minutes.
Maya proposes: Pairs could compare one line from the short text before we share anything with the whole group.
Noah proposes: A short demonstration could show newcomers what it means to give an interpretation and a reason.
The participant proposes: I suggest keeping time for questions about the club, using the information sheet for anything it actually answers.
Maya states partial support: I support showing an example, but I don't want it to take away the pair discussion.
Noah states partial support: I support some pair discussion. I still want us to decide how short the demonstration should be.
The participant states: I support protecting the question time. We still need a workable sequence within thirty minutes.
No complete sequence, stage durations or demonstration leader has been agreed. No taster has happened and no visitor result has been measured.

unknowns: The exact stage durations and whether an eventual detailed schedule fits
Who is willing and able to give the example
Which visitor questions the supplied information sheet will answer
Visitors' number, needs, preferences and willingness to share
Whether the group will adopt a complete proposal
How the activity would work in practice

baseline.meaning: All three proposals and the three explicit support statements are available as attributed source cards. The whole proposal remains open. Branch replies never become baseline facts.

proposal_check.proposal: We could begin with a brief example, use the same text in pairs, share one idea, and keep at least five minutes for club questions. Can we check the timing and who would give the example before we decide?
proposal_check.mayaReply: I support that sequence if the demonstration stays brief and the pair task remains.
proposal_check.noahReply: I support starting with an example and keeping question time. I am not ready to agree on the full sequence until we check the timings.
proposal_check.meaning: A labelled later authored check adds exactly these replies. Maya supports the sequence conditionally; Noah supports two elements and withholds support for the whole sequence pending timing. This does not establish a final group decision.

rehearsal.meaning: Use the explicit S05 proposal and replies as a frozen reference board, not as new speech to the learner. A private summary remains blank; the optional model is separate.

boundaries: Partial support attaches to a named element or condition; do not promote it to unconditional whole-group agreement.
No majority rule, unanimous decision procedure, assigned leader or final authority is supplied.
Thirty minutes is the activity duration, not a learner speaking limit or discussion deadline. The five-minute minimum is included, not added after thirty minutes.
At most twenty-five minutes remain for all other stages and transitions together, and fewer if question time exceeds five. This is a bound, not an agreed schedule.
A proposed demonstration leader is an unresolved dependency; do not assign Maya, Noah or an invisible facilitator without an authored decision.
The information sheet exists, but its complete contents are not supplied. Mark an unanswered question for checking; do not invent its answer.
Branch continuations and later model replies are authored examples, not observed real learner behaviour.
A coherent candidate can still need timing, accessibility and participation checks. Do not guarantee that a courteous summary wins agreement.

blocks.title: Use the Same Questions for Both Options
Protect a Requirement without Making a Promise
Distinguish a Reasoned Preference from a Decision

L08.S04.c001.speaker: coach
L08.S04.c001.text: When two arrangements compete, compare them against the same questions. In this taster, will newcomers have an opportunity to discuss the text? How will they find out about the club? Can the stages and transitions fit within thirty minutes while preserving the minimum question time? These questions come from this task, not a universal ranking system.
L08.S04.c001.visualEn: Open two candidate columns under one shared criterion row. Do not assign numerical quality scores.
L08.S04.c001.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S04.c001.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S04.c002.speaker: coach
L08.S04.c002.text: One candidate gives more room to a demonstration before pairs begin. Another keeps the example brief and leaves more room for participants to try. Neither description supplies exact durations yet. Compare the likely purpose and the possible cost, without treating those expectations as measured visitor outcomes.
L08.S04.c002.visualEn: Use flexible duration bands, not invented minute allocations. Both columns remain Candidate; expectations use may/could.
L08.S04.c002.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S04.c002.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S04.c003.speaker: coach
L08.S04.c003.text: A longer example may make the reasoning easier to inspect. It can also use minutes that would otherwise go to pairs, sharing or questions. You cannot preserve every stage at full size simply by calling the arrangement balanced. The total stays the same even when each element has a good reason.
L08.S04.c003.visualEn: One fixed30-minute container; optional bands expand/contract without implying a real chosen timetable.
L08.S04.c003.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S04.c003.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S04.c004.speaker: coach
L08.S04.c004.text: A useful trade-off statement connects an arrangement to the goal and names its limitation. You can prefer the briefer example because the task asks newcomers to try discussing the text. That preference still needs a check that the example is clear enough and that the pair task has a useful starting point.
L08.S04.c004.visualEn: Build a provisional preference card with purpose and check attached; preserve the need to try rather than only watch.
L08.S04.c004.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S04.c004.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S04.d001.speaker: learner
L08.S04.d001.text: I would keep the example brief so there is room to try the discussion in pairs. We still need to check that it shows the reasoning clearly.
L08.S04.d001.visualEn: Participant gives a concise preference and its limitation; no other character automatically agrees.
L08.S04.d001.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S04.d001.delivery: Natural collaborative speech; restrained gesture, no exaggerated conflict or comic voice.

L08.S04.c005.speaker: coach
L08.S04.c005.text: That statement does not claim a short example is always better. It explains why this candidate might fit this task. Someone can now question the link, suggest a clearer example or ask whether sharing needs a different place in the sequence. Those are useful revisions, not proof that the first speaker failed.
L08.S04.c005.visualEn: The same card remains editable; possible challenges attach to its reasoning rather than a character score.
L08.S04.c005.anchorHint: this candidate might fit this task
L08.S04.c005.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S04.c005.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S04.d002.speaker: noah
L08.S04.d002.text: I want the example to include a reason, not only an interpretation. Could we check that before deciding how brief it can be?
L08.S04.d002.visualEn: Noah offers an authored check in this excerpt; it does not establish a new source fact about the eventual demonstration.
L08.S04.d002.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S04.d002.delivery: Natural collaborative speech; restrained gesture, no exaggerated conflict or comic voice.

L08.S04.c006.speaker: coach
L08.S04.c006.text: That question helps define what must survive if the example is shortened. Keeping the reasoning visible is different from choosing the duration now. The group can look at a proposed example, check its essential content, and then consider how it affects the available time.
L08.S04.c006.visualEn: Separate essential content from duration decision. No actual completed demonstration or measured length appears.
L08.S04.c006.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S04.c006.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S04.c007.speaker: coach
L08.S04.c007.text: Apply the same care to the question period. At least five minutes is required; it is not evidence that five minutes will answer everything. If questions need longer, another part must fit into less time. Preserve the requirement while being honest about what the information sheet can answer.
L08.S04.c007.visualEn: Minimum-time label separate from answer-coverage label. Unknown visitor questions remain unresolved.
L08.S04.c007.anchorHint: not evidence that five minutes will answer everything
L08.S04.c007.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S04.c007.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S04.c008.speaker: coach
L08.S04.c008.text: Do not create a false choice between respect and selection. Taking someone's contribution seriously can mean preserving its purpose in a different form. It can also mean explaining why it does not fit this version. Respect does not require keeping every proposed detail unchanged.
L08.S04.c008.visualEn: Carry an attributed purpose card into a revised arrangement; if set aside, keep a small reason note, not a discarded-person icon.
L08.S04.c008.anchorHint: preserving its purpose in a different form
L08.S04.c008.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S04.c008.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S04.c009.speaker: coach
L08.S04.c009.text: A trade-off remains open to review when you say which assumption it depends on. Here, a brief example depends on someone being able and willing to provide it. If that is not established, the next step is to check or revise the candidate, not to announce that the arrangement is ready.
L08.S04.c009.visualEn: Attach a willingness/preparation check to the demonstration. No assigned role badge is generated.
L08.S04.c009.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S04.c009.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S04.c010.speaker: coach
L08.S04.c010.text: You can now explain a preference without presenting it as the group's decision. Keep the proposal, its purpose, its cost and its unresolved checks close together. A listener should not have to recover the caveat from a much earlier part of the discussion.
L08.S04.c010.visualEn: Create one compact candidate card with nearby conditions; keep a clearly visible Not adopted tag.
L08.S04.c010.anchorHint: without presenting it as the group
L08.S04.c010.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S04.c010.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S04.c011.speaker: coach
L08.S04.c011.text: Next, bring the candidate back to the group and ask about the support that matters. A useful check can reveal conditional support, a specific reservation or a need for more information. Each of those responses helps determine the next step without inventing a vote or a final authority.
L08.S04.c011.visualEn: End on a proposed check addressed to the group; no majority counter or leader crown.
L08.S04.c011.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S04.c011.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S04.h101.purpose: Privately name a benefit one candidate is intended to offer and a cost it could create.
L08.S04.h101.visualEn: Blank benefit/cost notes. Show no computed winner.

L08.S04.h102.purpose: Privately express one task-linked preference with its cost or unresolved condition.
L08.S04.h102.visualEn: Leave the response area blank. Show the criterion headings as optional prompts, not a required sentence formula.

boundary: Use formal explanation and short explicitly fictional excerpts. Partial support, open questions, candidate proposals and adopted decisions stay distinct. A summary does not create consent. Models are separate authored examples, not captured learner speech.
